items.note: It makes a clear call: stay on pgvector on RDS. It also says what would change that call (move to Qdrant, or to Pinecone/turbopuffer).
It works out storage for 5M×1536 vectors (≈30.7 GB float32, ≈15.4 GB halfvec) and projects growth to 9M and 13M at +1M per quarter.
The answer is built around the existing RDS PG 16 setup: low migration cost, the RDS pgvector version check, and reuse of current backups, IAM and monitoring.

Every cost cell is 'unknown', even for pgvector on RDS. It never checks any option against the $500/month limit and admits the budget is 'hard to assess'. It is honest about this, but the constraint is never applied.
Tenant filtering gets real attention: post-filtering in HNSW, iterative scans, partitioning by tenant_id, partial indexes, RLS, and filterable HNSW or namespaces for each option.
The comparison table has exactly 4 options. The 10-row wide scan is a separate screening step, and the brief asked for one.
It gives a 4-option comparison table plus one clear recommendation.
It retrieved no sources, and every date is 'unknown'. It says so openly, but it can't show any preference for sources from the last 12 months.

The wide scan is done and two options are named for deep dives, but only pgvector gets real depth. Qdrant's 'deep dive' is one table row with no pricing, figures or details beyond what Pinecone and turbopuffer get, so the second deep dive is basically missing.
